symbols.name: base-2 logarithm
symbols.meaning: The base-2 logarithm, the function the page writes as log.
symbols.quote: The n log n optimality conjecture says that no method of multiplying two integers can take asymptotically less time than $n \log n$, where $\log$ is the base-2 logarithm and $n$ is the number of bits in each input.

symbols.name: eventual threshold
symbols.meaning: The input length from which the lower bound for machine A is required to hold.
symbols.quote: The conjecture says that for every such machine $A$ there are a positive constant $c_A$ and a threshold $N_A$ on the input length such that the following holds.

symbols.name: threshold input length
symbols.meaning: A threshold on the input length, from which the negated statement asks for some input length with a small running time ratio.
symbols.quote: For every positive $\varepsilon$ and every threshold $n_0$ on the input length, there is some $n \ge n_0$ with $T_A(n) < \varepsilon\, n \lg n$.

relations.quote: The conjecture bounds the cost of [exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) from below.
The conjecture is negated through the [limit inferior](limit-inferior.md) of the ratio $T_A(n)/(n\lg n)$.
